messages:
amanda: FYI I put up an RFC for on-prem packaging + operator API tradeoffs — please skim when you have a minute: https://rfc.redwood.local/r/onprem-packaging-api (short summary in thread)

amanda: tl;dr: aim for minimal operator surface (activate/apply/inspect), push complex heuristics to control-plane tooling, and keep bundle format optimistic for streaming installs.

devon: quick q — how do we guarantee atomic upgrades when customers are offline for hours?

raj: prefer a two-phase: staged-download + staged-activation. download is resumable; activation is a single switch with preflight probes. if preflight fails, operator stays in pending and we expose an explicit rollback API.

natalie: concern: what about key rotation and attestation when the control plane can't reach the environment? KMS calls are a no-go in strict air-gap.

amanda: agreed. design assumes customer-managed signing (HSM/KMS) locally. bundles are signed by a rotating signer and include a signer-chain file. operator verifies chain locally.

devon: ok — and delta bundles? do we force full-image swaps or support binary deltas?

raj: deltas ok but only if there is a manifest that lets operator validate content-addressed chunks. otherwise fallback to full image. deltas add resume complexity but save bandwidth for large models.

natalie: also need explicit operator API for admin-confirmation. if activation would change runtime ABI (quantization change, backend swap), operator should surface an "unsafe_changes" field and require admin ack.

amanda: yes — plan in RFC: operator API endpoints: POST /apply {manifest, options}, GET /status, POST /rollback, GET /verify. options includes apply-window, admin-ack token, and allow-partial-activation:false by default.

raj: example operator config snippet I pasted in the RFC:
```yaml
operator:
  allow_partial_apply: false
  apply_window_seconds: 300
  max_concurrent_applies: 1
  verifier: local-signer-chain
```

devon: rough perf question — verifying local signature chain for every chunk will spike CPU on low-end nodes. do we do sampling or cached-attestations? :thinking:

natalie: proposal: verify manifest + a sampled set of chunks on apply, then background-verify remainder. operator marks bundle as "partially-verified" until done. critical for CPU-constrained appliances.

amanda: fallback heuristics: if background verify fails we mark object degraded and auto-disable new traffic routing (console-level flag). Also add automatic retry+exponential backoff and manual override API.

raj: quick log example for telemetry keys we want:
```
[apply:start] manifest=sha256:abcd, size=42GB, mode=delta
[verify:sampled] chunks=128/16384 duration=12s
[apply:activate] result=pending, admin_ack=false
```

sre-bot: deploy-bot: RFC doc registered and reviewers pinged: amanda, devon, natalie. :white_check_mark:

devon: cool — can we also add a compatibility matrix for operator versions vs bundle schema versions? that's been a recurring pain.

amanda: yes — I'll add a compact matrix and an example upgrade path (operator v1.2 -> v1.3 with schema v2 fallback) and call out migration steps. planning to iterate RFC tomorrow. @devon @natalie please review the API examples and signer-chain layout when you get a chance. :pray:
